chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah from 'Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:

I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon them both): regarding the verse 'There is no blame upon you [O Muslims] that you eat from the houses of your fathers or the houses of your grandfathers,' [what is the ruling]?
He said: 'There is no blame upon you regarding what you have tasted or eaten from that of which you possess the keys, as long as you do not corrupt it.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ: There is no blame upon you
key_terms.مَا لَمْ تُفْسِدْهُ: As long as you do not corrupt it

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for eating from one's ancestral home according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the condition of 'ownership' in Quran 2:215 by linking it to the possession of keys (*mafatih*), a key concept in Shia jurisprudence for establishing exclusive control over property. The Imam further specifies that the permission to consume is valid provided the food is not corrupted (*fasad*), thereby refining the scope of lawful consumption beyond mere possession to include the integrity of the item. This hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the intersection of property rights and dietary laws in Shia fiqh.
